data_fields.name: clip frame time (fps per clip)
data_fields.donor_constant: frameLerp = 1000 / fps, fps from the model's animation.cfg

data_fields.name: clip start delay
data_fields.donor_constant: initialLerp = 1000 / fps (one frame); animationTime = frameTime + initialLerp

data_fields.name: swing speed
data_fields.donor_constant: cg_swingSpeed default 0.3, times frametime and band scale

data_fields.name: swing band factors
data_fields.donor_constant: 0.5 below half tolerance, 1.0 below tolerance, 2.0 above

best_idea: Give each actor one clip clock that schedules frame times from the previous frame time (not the wall clock), starts a new clip after one frame of delay, and blends the old frame into the new with one backlerp weight, so every clip switch and every part attachment reads one number.
decision_why: Frankendom's hero and creature clips need the clock rules (scheduled frame times, one step per call, one-frame start delay, hold-then-next, the 200 ms guard) and a single backlerp weight; the MD3 vertex morph and the matrix blend are not needed with Three.js skinning. Client-side only.
acceptance: A Pit hero that switches from guard to strike starts the strike clip one clip frame after the command and blends from the guard's last frame over that frame; a unit test feeds fake times to advance() and asserts frame and backlerp at 0 ms, one frame and 1000 ms after a stall.
